transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2029-04-11 16:00 UTC
Duration: ~56 minutes
Attendees: Maya Chen (Redwood AE), Lucas Ortega (Redwood SE), Priya Rao (CTO, Oryx), Daniel Sloane (Lead ML Eng), Marcus Li (Infra)

Auto-summary:
We ran through Oryx's production targets (p95 targets, concurrency expectations for multi-tenant inference, streaming behavior for chat-like flows). Oryx is evaluating Redwood hosting modes: Hosted for fast time-to-prod, Dedicated for predictable throughput, Private for data residency and air-gapped controls. Key ask: how to guarantee sub-400ms p95 for 16-token responses and sub-800ms for 128-token streams under 200 concurrent users with graceful degrade to cheaper model variants.

[00:00] Maya: hey everyone, thanks for joining. we did the invite, can you hear me okay?
[00:05] Priya: yes, hearing you fine.
[00:07] Lucas: great, i'll share the agenda quick — p95 targets, traffic profile, streaming behavior, fallback options, then action items.
[00:15] Priya: sounds good. to set context we run an assistant in our clinical portal — mostly short answers (8-30 tokens) but occasionally longer summaries (~150 tokens) for discharge notes. Our latency SLO is tight because clinicians expect fast responses.
[00:28] Daniel: and we see bursts during shift changes — 5-10x baseline for 2-5 minutes. So concurrency spikes are real.
[00:36] Marcus: infra constraints: we need audit logs and KMS integration, probably VPC for the private option.
[00:41] Maya: great, do you have a target p95 number you measure against today?
[00:46] Priya: we call it 300 to 400ms for quick answers. 300 is ideal but 400 is acceptable. for longer generation we can tolerate up to 800-900ms p95.
[00:57] Lucas: ok that's useful. quick clarification — when you say 300-400ms is that end-to-end from portal request to first token arriving on client?
[01:04] Priya: yes, first token delivered to the UI. streaming first byte matters.
[01:10] Lucas: good. on Redwood hosted we typically can hit sub-200ms for short prompts on optimized kernels for smaller open models. for streaming we optimize the initial token path separate from sustained token/sec.
[01:22] Daniel: can you explain the difference between initial token p95 and steady-state throughput?
[01:26] Lucas: sure, initial token p95 is influenced by model load time, cold starts, routing and any prefix cache lookups — we do KV cache and prefix caching. steady-state token/sec is about how many tokens per second the runtime emits once generation is running — that depends on batch size, quantization, and hardware.
[01:40] Priya: we are sensitive to cold starts. can you guarantee no cold starts during bursts?
[01:44] Maya: with Dedicated you get reserved GPU pools, autoscaling, and warm instances — that reduces cold-start variability. Hosted has burst-optimized pools but might fall back to slightly higher-latency variants during extreme surge.
[01:54] Marcus: what about Private in our VPC? we prefer full control but worried about ops overhead.
[01:59] Lucas: Private gives you the same runtime but in your network — you manage nodes. Redwood provides deployment tooling, but yes ops overhead is higher. we can provide an opinionated helm chart and an initial runbook.
[02:10] Priya: can you talk about graceful fallback? e.g., if the preferred model can't keep up, can it switch to a cheaper smaller model automatically?
[02:16] Lucas: yes, policy-driven fallbacks are supported. you can route by latency, cost, or region. e.g., primary model L-XL for quality, fallback to L-M for high concurrency. we also do response shaping to limit token count.
[02:28] Daniel: how do you measure p95 in streaming? do you measure first-byte p95 and completion p95 separately?
[02:33] Lucas: yep. first-byte p95, and tail p95 for completion. For monitoring we provide token-level tracing and cost breakdowns per request. you can create alerts on first-byte p95 breaches.
[02:42] Priya: our traffic pattern — baseline 40 concurrent users, surges to ~200 concurrent for 3-6 minutes twice daily. average quick-answers are 12 tokens, long summaries 120 tokens.
[02:53] Maya: ok, that helps. rough capacity math — for 200 concurrent with streaming, what throughput do you need in token/sec?
[02:59] Daniel: assuming average 12 tokens and we stream first token quickly, the steady state token/sec is modest but peak token bursts when multiple long responses align can be significant. We can provide a traffic sample.
[03:14] Lucas: request that sample, please — sample prompts + concurrency timeline will let us propose model + instance mixes.
[03:18] Priya: we'll share that.
[03:20] Marcus: security — SOC 2 and KMS, do you support customer-managed keys?
[03:24] Maya: yes, Hosted supports CMK integration with our key-wrapping, Dedicated and Private of course integrate with your KMS/HSM. we'll include SOC 2 summary in the pack.
[03:34] Daniel: what about multi-tenancy isolation? we don't want other tenants noisy neighbors to affect our p95.
[03:39] Lucas: Dedicated is single-tenant GPU pools which gives isolation. Hosted offers soft guarantees with prioritization and reserved burst capacity for higher tiers. for strict isolation, Dedicated or Private.
[03:49] Priya: can Redwood run our benchmark harness? we'd like to see realistic p95 numbers on your infra with our prompts.
[03:54] Maya: yes. we usually do an SE-run benchmark using your sample prompts and our harness; we can run hosted + dedicated variants and supply a spreadsheet with p50/p95/p99 and token/sec numbers.
[04:03] Daniel: do you provide an open-source harness or is it internal? we want something reproducible.
[04:07] Lucas: we will provide the harness scripts and a containerized test runner — reproducible. we'll also commit to a config you can run in your env for Private.
[04:16] Priya: curious about model quantization — will quantization affect answer quality? we need clinical precision.
[04:21] Lucas: yes it can, depends on model. we recommend tuning: some models quantize well without measurable quality drop, others need evals. Redwood Optimize can suggest quantization profiles per workload and tie regressions to prompt tests.
[04:34] Maya: i'd like to talk about specific SLO numbers we'll aim for in the POC. propose first-byte p95 <= 350ms for short responses, completion p95 <= 800ms for long responses, and 95% of bursts handled without fallback.
[04:47] Priya: that sounds reasonable. if you can show that on the benchmark, we can move forward to a pilot.
[04:51] Lucas: one more technical note — when we say streaming p95 we'll need to instrument client-side metrics (time-to-first-byte) and server traces. do you have telemetry currently in the portal?
[04:59] Marcus: we have basic APM traces and Sentry. we can push a small agent or SDK.
[05:04] Daniel: what about batching? will batching to improve token/sec impact first-byte latency?
[05:09] Lucas: continuous batching is dynamic — we batch where it helps but we keep an inline fast-path for small short requests to preserve first-byte latency. there's an ops knob for exchange between throughput and latency.
[05:20] Priya: can we set a policy so quick answers never get batched?
[05:23] Lucas: yes, you can set thresholds by expected token length/time-sensitivity.
[05:28] Maya: ok, let's sketch the pilot: 2-week POC, run on Dedicated reserved pool sized for 200 concurrent with auto-burst; Redwood runs benchmark with your sample traffic; we'll compare Hosted and Dedicated p95 and show fallback transitions under overload.
[05:41] Priya: what's pricing for a Dedicated pool for a 2-week pilot?
[05:45] Maya: for pilot we usually offer trial pricing — we'll include a short-term commit quote; if you go production we can convert to a monthly committed capacity. I'll follow up in the pricing doc.
[05:54] Daniel: questions about routing — if we have spike in EU region, can you route to US fallback? we have data residency constraints for PHI.
[06:01] Lucas: automatic cross-region fallback is possible but for PHI you probably want to avoid leaving region. We can do same-region fallbacks to smaller model variants first, then manual cross-region as last resort — configurable.
[06:13] Marcus: audit logs retention — if we run Dedicated how long are logs kept and can we push to our SIEM?
[06:18] Maya: yes, we support push of audit logs, and retention can be customized for enterprise contracts.
[06:24] Priya: last topic — demo? we'd like a short demo of streaming first-byte and a simulated burst.
[06:29] Maya: sure we can do a follow-up demo. that would be an SE-led session with the harness.
[06:33] Lucas: action items summarize — i'll prepare the harness and run the benchmark; Maya will send security and pricing; Priya/Daniel will upload prompts and traffic profile.
[06:40] Priya: yep. thanks, this was productive.
[06:44] Maya: great, we'll follow up with meeting notes and schedule the benchmark session.
[06:49] Daniel: one small thing, can you include a sample model matrix with expected p95s per GPU type?
[06:53] Lucas: yes, we'll include a matrix: model variants, quantization option, GPU type, expected p50/p95, token/sec.
[06:59] Maya: perfect. thanks everyone.

End of transcript.
